name: INCB123667
summary: INCB123667 is Incyte's oral, selective CDK2 inhibitor, with no INN yet. The lead trial is MAESTRA 2 (NCT07214779, ENGOT-OV95 / GOG-3137): a randomised, open-label Phase 3 of INCB123667 against investigator's choice chemotherapy in about 466 women with platinum-resistant high-grade serous ovarian cancer that overexpresses cyclin E1 (IHC, at least 75% of tumour cells at 1+ or more), after 1 to 4 prior lines. PFS by blinded central review and OS are the primary endpoints, and primary completion is 2028-11. A single-arm Phase 2 (MAESTRA 1, NCT07023627, ORR primary, completion 2027-04) could support an earlier accelerated filing. A first-line maintenance Phase 3 with bevacizumab (MAESTRA 3, NCT07797283, completion 2032-05) is not modelled. Price anchor: Lifyorli (relacorilant), the oral drug FDA approved in March 2026 for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer after 1 to 3 prior lines, at a WAC of $37,900 per 28-day cycle, $494,054 a year. Uptake anchor: none can be solved. Elahere, the only biomarker-selected incumbent, has no CMS row in the book and no patient count in any filing, so peak penetration is null and the ramp reuses the book's Enhertu fit, as the two other platinum-resistant ovarian seeds do. Second reader: 13 fields confirmed, 1 corrected, none withdrawn. gross_to_net_pct is now Incyte's own filed FY2025 gross-to-net, 0.3229, in place of the Kalydeco ratio (0.2777), which the book itself calls a floor. Net price is $334,524 a year. Peak penetration stays null. Elahere's US revenue has been flat since H1 2025 at about $160mm a quarter, but it implies roughly 3,100 to 4,100 courses a year. That is about twice the FRa-high share of the book's platinum-resistant pool (about 1,590). A real-world cohort also puts 48% of Elahere use outside platinum-resistant disease. So the capture cannot be solved. Three new facts from the MAESTRA 2 design, found by search: the dose is 50 mg twice daily, prior bevacizumab is required, and FRa-positive patients must have had prior mirvetuximab. Elahere therefore comes a line before this asset rather than competing with it.

therapy_mode.source: NCT07214779 (book trials table: randomised, PFS by BICR primary); MAESTRA 2 trial-in-progress abstract, ASCO 2026 (J Clin Oncol 2026;44(16_suppl):TPS5642, doi:10.1200/JCO.2026.44.16_suppl.TPS5642): oral INCB123667 against investigator's choice chemotherapy, PFS and OS dual primary endpoints. Phase 1 dosing 50 or 100 mg daily (INCB123667 phase 1 (NCT05238922) in platinum-resistant and refractory ovarian cancer, ASCO 2025 abstract 5514 (J Clin Oncol 2025;43(16_suppl):5514, doi:10.1200/JCO.2025.43.16_suppl.5514; reported by Targeted Oncology, https://www.targetedonc.com/view/novel-cdk2-inhibitor-incb123667-shows-promise-in-ovarian-cancer))
therapy_mode.note: Oral daily dosing until progression, so chronic by the house definition
therapy_mode.check: Book trials table: NCT07214779 is randomised, primary outcome 'PFS by BICR', 466 patients, start 2025-12-09. Search (ASCO TPS5642 page, OncLive) confirms oral INCB123667 against investigator's choice of weekly paclitaxel, PLD, gemcitabine or topotecan. The Phase 3 dose is 50 mg twice daily, not the phase 1's 50 or 100 mg once daily that the source cites. It is still continuous oral dosing to progression, so 'chronic' holds. OS as a second primary endpoint was not visible in any extract; only PFS by BICR is confirmed.

list_price_per_patient.source: Lifyorli (relacorilant, Corcept) WAC of $37,900 per 28-day cycle (Fierce Pharma, https://www.fiercepharma.com/pharma/corcepts-lead-drug-bounces-back-fda-snub-1st-approval-lifyorli-ovarian-cancer). 37,900 x 365/28 = $494,054 a year. FDA approval 2026-03-25, with nab-paclitaxel, for platinum-resistant epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer after 1 to 3 prior lines including bevacizumab (Corcept release, https://ir.corcept.com/news-releases/news-release-details/fda-approves-corcepts-selective-glucocorticoid-receptor; OCRA, https://ocrahope.org/news/slug-fda-approves-lifyorli-relacorilant-platinum-resistant-ovarian-cancer/)
list_price_per_patient.note: Judgement on the comparator. Lifyorli is the closest marketed comparator in disease, setting and route: an oral drug approved for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer after 1 to 3 prior lines, the patients MAESTRA 2 enrols (1 to 4). It has a named manufacturer list price, which the brief puts ahead of the CMS convention, and it launched too late for a CMS row. The velzatinib seed annualises a per-pack WAC the same way (Qinlock). Case against, three parts. (1) The WAC is for relacorilant alone, dosed around nab-paclitaxel, which is billed on top; a monotherapy could price above or below it. (2) Elahere, the biomarker-selected incumbent, has only a per-vial WAC ($6,487.15, AbbVie Colorado disclosure, as the sofetabart second reader found): 3 to 4 vials a 21-day cycle is about $19,500 to $26,000, or roughly $340,000 to $450,000 a year, so this anchor sits at or above the class. (3) The engine bills a full year's price to every patient in the treated stock, new starts included. At a constant hazard with a 5.3-month median PFS, mean time on drug is about 7.6 months, so WAC per start is about $315,000, while the engine books 494,054 / 0.7918 = about $624,000 per start at list, roughly twice. The CMS convention absorbs this because spend per beneficiary is already a part-year figure. The nearest CMS figure is Zejula, the oral ovarian PARP inhibitor, at $111,182 per Part D beneficiary in 2024 (lookup.py demand Zejula: $224,142,913 over 2,016). It is first-line maintenance, a different setting, and would understate this line by more than this anchor overstates it
list_price_per_patient.check: Search (Fierce Pharma, the URL cited) confirms the Lifyorli WAC: $37,900 per 28-day cycle, covering nine relacorilant doses (the day before, of and after each nab-paclitaxel infusion), so the drug is dosed intermittently. Search (OCRA, CancerNetwork) confirms the approval: FDA 2026-03-25, with nab-paclitaxel, PROC after 1 to 3 prior lines including bevacizumab; ROSELLA PFS 6.5 vs 5.5 months. Arithmetic: 37,900 x 365/28 = $494,054, so 0.494054 mm USD per patient-year is right. Elahere annual WAC at $6,487.15 a vial (AbbVie CO disclosure, as the sofetabart reader saw it) x 3 to 4 vials x 365/21 = $338,259 to $451,011, as the note says. Zejula: $224,142,913 / 2,016 = $111,182 (lookup.py demand). The judgement stands: this is a published annual list price in the same disease and line. Three points strengthen the case against. (1) MAESTRA 2 needs prior mirvetuximab if FRa-positive, so this asset treats later than Lifyorli's 1 to 3 lines. (2) The WAC buys nine intermittent doses a cycle, against continuous 50 mg twice-daily dosing. (3) The per-start overbilling is real in the engine. forecast.py treated_stock uses stock(t) = stock(t-1) x (1 - d) + new(t) and bills stock x annual net price. At d = 0.7918 that is 494,054 / 0.7918 = $623,963 at list per start, against about $315,022 expected (mean 7.65 months on drug at a constant hazard, 8.31 cycles). That is 1.98x. It is an engine property rather than a price error, but revenue per patient here is about double.

gross_to_net_pct.source: Incyte FY2025 10-K (0000879169-26-000010), MD&A sales allowances table, read from the book's filing_sections. Allowances for current-period sales were $2,091.893mm and prior-period adjustments -$15.397mm, so $2,076.496mm came off. Total product revenues, net, were $4,354.3mm, which makes gross (WAC-invoiced) sales $6,430.796mm. 2,076.496 / 6,430.796 = 0.3229
gross_to_net_pct.note: Judgement: the seller's own measured gross-to-net over its whole product line, used because a WAC anchor takes neither house convention and needs a sourced discount. Jakafi, an oral haematology-oncology drug sold through specialty pharmacy, is 71% of the net ($3,092.5mm). Direction checked: 32.29% comes off list, so net is 494,054 x 0.6771 = $334,524 a patient-year. Range from the same tables: FY2024 0.3062 ((1,589.621 + 7.465) / (3,618.9 + 1,597.086), 10-K 0001628280-25-004633). FY2025 without the Opzelura line-extension accrual build ($127.6mm to $218.5mm, reversed after the 2026 CMS settlement) is 0.3088. H1 2026 without the settlement is about 0.35 (10-Q 0000879169-26-000056). Case for lower: Jakafi's government rebates carry an inflation penalty that a new launch does not (Incyte says so in the same section), and Opzelura's commercial co-pay spending is heavy. Case for higher: the rate has risen each period since 2024. The portfolio also includes some ex-US sales with European mandated discounts. The researcher's Kalydeco ratio (0.2777) is the book's floor and mostly measures part-year fills, per vrtx_prices.csv and gross_to_net.py.
gross_to_net_pct.check: The old value's arithmetic holds but its source is weak. Kalydeco CMS Part D 2024: $28,727,989 / 105 = $273,600. WAC $29,057.52 x 365/28 = $378,786. 1 - 273,600 / 378,786 = 0.2777, as on the velzatinib, dazukibart and VX-147 seeds. But vrtx_prices.csv calls it a FLOOR, and backend/gross_to_net.py explains that spending per beneficiary is below a year of therapy because of part-year fills, so the ratio does not measure rebates. Incyte files a direct measure of what comes off its own WAC. The FY2025 table was read in the book's copy of 10-K 0000879169-26-000010: allowances for current-period sales 229,701 + 1,692,462 + 146,685 + 23,045 = 2,091,893 ($000), prior-period -15,397, net product revenues $4,354.3mm. That gives 0.3229 all-in. FY2024 gives 0.3062, and H1 2026 about 0.35 without the $246mm Opzelura settlement. Every period is above 0.2777, the direction the book's own note predicts. 0.2777 -> 0.3229: net price falls from $356,855 to $334,524 a patient-year (-6.3%).

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: INCB123667 phase 1 (NCT05238922) in platinum-resistant and refractory ovarian cancer, ASCO 2025 abstract 5514 (J Clin Oncol 2025;43(16_suppl):5514, doi:10.1200/JCO.2025.43.16_suppl.5514; reported by Targeted Oncology, https://www.targetedonc.com/view/novel-cdk2-inhibitor-incb123667-shows-promise-in-ovarian-cancer): median PFS 5.3 months across the 50 and 100 mg daily groups (n = 30); ORR 33.3%
discontinuation_pct.note: Constant hazard from a median: 1 - 0.5^(12/5.3) = 0.792, the form the vepugratinib and velzatinib seeds use. The brief's 1 - exp(-12/5.3) gives 0.896 because it treats the median as a mean; the sofetabart seed in this disease used that form (0.882 on MIRASOL's 5.62 months). Case for higher: at 100 mg alone (n = 14) median PFS was 4.5 months (0.842) and median duration of response 3.6 months, and time on drug usually runs shorter than PFS. Case for lower: phase 1 patients had a median of 4 prior lines, more than many MAESTRA 2 patients will have, and Lifyorli plus nab-paclitaxel ran a median PFS of 6.5 months in ROSELLA (OCRA, URL under list_price_per_patient). A single-arm phase 1 of 30 patients is a thin base
discontinuation_pct.check: Search (OncLive; Targeted Oncology, the URL cited; ASCO abstract 5514 page) confirms median PFS 5.3 months across the 50 and 100 mg once-daily groups (n = 30) and median duration of response 3.6 months. Arithmetic: 1 - 0.5^(12/5.3) = 0.7918; the brief's form gives 0.8961; 4.5 months gives 0.8425. All hold. The 4.5-month figure for 100 mg alone (n = 14) was not seen in an extract. It appears only in the note. The constant-hazard-from-median form matches the velzatinib and vepugratinib seeds. Caveat to carry: the Phase 3 dose is 50 mg twice daily, a schedule the phase 1 PFS does not directly measure. Real-world Elahere, the prior line for FRa-positive patients, ran a median PFS of 5.3 months (PMID 42733650), consistent with this range.

forecast_start_year.source: NCT07214779 primary completion 2028-11-15, estimated (context file; book trials table, last update 2026-09-15)
forecast_start_year.note: Judgement on the timeline: readout around the turn of 2029, filing in 2029 and a US launch late in 2029, so 2030 is the first full year. The sofetabart and AZD5335 seeds in this setting also start in 2030. Case for earlier: in September 2024 Incyte named an accelerated filing on the single-arm Phase 2 as one scenario, pending FDA feedback (ApexOnco, https://www.oncologypipeline.com/apexonco/incyte-goes-pivotal-cdk2). MAESTRA 1 (NCT07023627, 160 patients, ORR by independent review, primary completion 2027-04-27) would then put launch in 2028 and the first full year in 2029, with MAESTRA 2 already enrolling as the confirmatory trial. Case against that path: median duration of response at 100 mg was 3.6 months in phase 1
forecast_start_year.check: Book trials table: NCT07214779 primary completion 2028-11-15 (estimated), completion 2029-05-14. NCT07023627 (MAESTRA 1) primary completion 2027-04-27, 160 patients, ORR by IRC. Incyte 10-Q 0000879169-26-000056 confirms both started in Q4 2025. With a readout in early 2029, a filing in 2029 and launch around the turn of 2030, 2030 as the first full year is on the early side but defensible. It matches the sofetabart and AZD5335 seeds (both 2030, lookup.py seed). The ApexOnco claim of an accelerated-filing scenario was not re-checked; it sits only in the note.

exus_multiple.source: Elahere FY2025: United States $607mm, International $83mm (ABBV FY2025 10-K 0001551152-26-000008, as carried on the book's mirvetuximab base_revenue row, lookup.py seed mirvetuximab). 83 / 607 = 0.137
exus_multiple.note: Judgement on the comparator. Elahere is the biomarker-selected incumbent in the same line, and the sofetabart seed uses the same split, so the book's platinum-resistant ovarian seeds stay on one basis. Incyte sells its own products in Europe and Japan (Opzelura ran 0.237 in FY2025, 10-K 0000879169-26-000010). Case for higher: Elahere's EU approval came only in November 2024, so this is an early split. Zejula, a mature oral ovarian drug, runs 0.908 (GSK FY2025: US 292, Europe 215, International 50, annual report 0001654954-26-000892, in the book's asset_revenue_regions), though its US use shrank after the 2022 US label restriction. Note that the engine scales the patient pool by this multiple at the US price
exus_multiple.check: lookup.py seed mirvetuximab and product_revenue.csv: ABBV FY2025 10-K 0001551152-26-000008, Elahere US 607, International 83. 83 / 607 = 0.1367. The sofetabart seed carries the same value. Opzelura: the book has International $130mm of $678.455mm total, so 130 / 548.455 = 0.237. Zejula GSK FY2025: (215 + 50) / 292 = 0.908 (asset_revenue_regions). Both hold. New evidence for the stated case for higher: ABBV 10-Q 0001551152-26-000026 (product_revenue.csv) gives Elahere H1 2026 US 321 and International 88, so 0.274, and Q2 2026 50 / 161 = 0.311. The ex-US split doubled within six months of the FY2025 figure. Kept at the latest full filed year for consistency with the sofetabart seed; a mature split is likely higher.

economics_share.source: Incyte release, 'Incyte's CDK2 Inhibitor INCB123667 Shows Promising Evidence of Clinical Activity in Patients with Advanced Solid Tumors, Notably Ovarian Cancer' (https://investor.incyte.com/news-releases/news-release-details/incytes-cdk2-inhibitor-incb123667-shows-promising-evidence). Incyte is lead sponsor of all five trials in the context file and of the phase 1 NCT05238922 (book trials table)

The book's deals, reported_deals and news tables have no INCB123667 licence. The book trials table shows Incyte as lead sponsor of NCT07214779, NCT07023627, NCT07797283 and NCT05238922. 1.0 holds.

prevalence.note: lookup.py pool 'Ovarian Neoplasms': the R-DXD row carries 21,010 (SEER Cancer Stat Facts, ovary, 2026 estimate) for prevalence and incidence. Used as is
prevalence.check: lookup.py pool 'Ovarian Neoplasms': the R-DXD row carries 21,010 (SEER, ovary, 2026 estimate) for both prevalence and incidence, so null with 'carried by the book' is right.

incidence.check: As prevalence: the book carries 21,010 a year.

eligible_pct.source: Two filters. (1) Platinum-resistant patients treated in lines 2 to 4: 4,382 a year, 0.2086 of the book's 21,010, from ISPOR 2024 poster 139151 / Value in Health HSD30 (https://www.valueinhealthjournal.com/article/S1098-3015(24)01368-8/fulltext): 6,224, 4,329 and 2,901 patients treated in lines 2, 3 and 4 in 2023, of whom 14.7%, 40.5% and 59.1% were platinum-resistant. It is the share the sofetabart seed carries, confirmed by its second reader. (2) Cyclin E1 overexpression in 83 of 90 (92.2%) ovarian cancer patients in the INCB123667 phase 1 (NCT05238922) in platinum-resistant and refractory ovarian cancer, ASCO 2025 abstract 5514 (J Clin Oncol 2025;43(16_suppl):5514, doi:10.1200/JCO.2025.43.16_suppl.5514; reported by Targeted Oncology, https://www.targetedonc.com/view/novel-cdk2-inhibitor-incb123667-shows-promise-in-ovarian-cancer). 0.2086 x 0.922 = 0.1923, about 4,040 women a year
eligible_pct.note: Judgement on the biomarker share. MAESTRA 2's cutoff is permissive: at least 75% of tumour cells at IHC 1+ or more (TPS5642). No paper reports prevalence at that cutoff; the phase 1 figure is Incyte's own population but may not use the same definition. The phase 1 was enriched for CCNE1 amplification (56.7%, against about 20% expected in a platinum-resistant trial population per Kim et al., NPJ Precis Oncol 2026, doi:10.1038/s41698-026-01519-6). Re-weighting to 20% amplification gives 0.86 if every amplified tumour overexpresses and 0.94 if 90% do, which brackets 0.922. Case for lower: stricter cutoffs find 51% (azenosertib's clinical cutoff) to 59% (H-score 145 or more) in platinum-resistant trial cohorts (Kim et al. 2026); 42% after neoadjuvant chemotherapy and 61% after a PARP inhibitor at H-score 150 or more (Trecourt et al., Br J Cancer 2026;135:427, doi:10.1038/s41416-026-03440-y); and 22.4% of 3,029 tumours at the OTTA cutoff, mostly at diagnosis (Kang et al., Cancer 2023;129:697, doi:10.1002/cncr.34582). At 0.51 the share would be 0.1064. MAESTRA 2 also requires high-grade serous histology, which the ISPOR counts do not filter. High-grade serous is about 70% of all ovarian cancer (Kim et al.) and more of stage III/IV disease, so this overstates by the non-serous share of advanced platinum-resistant disease, for which no sourced figure was found. Case for higher: MAESTRA 2 admits a fourth prior line (line 5), which lines 2 to 4 leave out. The ISPOR counts are treatment events, so one patient can appear in two lines
eligible_pct.check: Arithmetic: 0.2086 x 83/90 (0.9222) = 0.1924, or 0.2086 x 0.922 = 0.1923, about 4,040 a year on 21,010. 0.2086 is the sofetabart seed's ISPOR row (lookup.py pool), whose per-line counts that seed's second reader confirmed. Search (Targeted Oncology / ASCO 5514) confirms cyclin E1 overexpression in 83 of 90 (92.2%) and CCNE1 amplification in 51 (56.7%), with a median of 4 prior lines. Search (TPS5642, ASCO page) confirms the cutoff: at least 75% of tumour cells at IHC 1+ or more, high-grade serous, 1 to 4 prior lines. Re-weighting: non-amplified overexpression is 32/39 = 0.8205, giving 0.2 + 0.8 x 0.8205 = 0.856; at 90% of amplified tumours, 0.94. Both hold. Sources in the note confirmed on PubMed: Kim et al. 2026 (PMID 42218323), 59% overexpressed; Trecourt et al. 2026 (PMID 42086671), 42% post-NACT and 61% post-PARPi at H-score 150 or more; Kang et al. 2023 (PMID 36572991), 22.4% of 3,029. Kim's 51% at the azenosertib cutoff and the 20% amplification figure were not in the abstract. 0.2086 x 0.51 = 0.1064. Two label filters the note leaves out, neither sourced enough to apply. (1) MAESTRA 2 requires prior bevacizumab, which the ISPOR counts do not filter (the phase 1 had 76.7% prior bevacizumab, a heavily pretreated group); this pushes the share down. (2) FRa-positive patients must have had prior mirvetuximab. Kim et al. put 33% of cyclin E1-positive tumours at FRa-high, so those patients reach this drug one line later, some in line 5, which ISPOR lines 2 to 4 exclude. Judgement stands as labelled.

untreated_carryover_pct.source: forecast.py convention for a line of cancer therapy (patients_for_indication)
untreated_carryover_pct.note: A patient not started on this drug in a year starts another regimen and leaves the line. The book's pool has prevalence equal to incidence (21,010), so the engine would infer zero on its own; stated to make it explicit
untreated_carryover_pct.check: backend/forecast.py (lines 162-190): a pool whose prevalence equals incidence gets carryover 0 by default. Stating 0.0 explicitly matches the line-of-therapy convention, and the book's pool is 21,010 = 21,010.

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of each year's eligible patients
penetration_peak_pct.note: The biomarker-selected incumbent in this line is Elahere. The book has no CMS row for it, and neither AbbVie's nor ImmunoGen's filings report a patient count (the sofetabart second reader searched ImmunoGen's 2023 8-Ks and AbbVie's 10-K). Three searches here for a real-world share of eligible patients treated with Elahere, or for a patient count from ImmunoGen's 2023 calls, found none. Lifyorli launched in March 2026 and has no uptake data yet. EV+P's 51% of first-line urothelial patients (the vepugratinib anchor) is another disease. Left null, so the engine draws its placeholder curve and keeps the asset out of per-share value until a sourced figure exists. Next step: load Elahere (HCPCS J9063) from the CMS Part B Spending by Drug file into drug_demand and solve against the FRa-high share of the ISPOR pool
penetration_peak_pct.check: Null upheld after the requested Elahere attempt. No measured capture exists. (1) No CMS row: book drug_demand has no Elahere or mirvetuximab rows (ends 2024), data.cms.gov is blocked (403), and a search for J9063 Part B beneficiaries found none. (2) No patient count or share: searches of ImmunoGen's 2023 8-Ks, earnings coverage and AbbVie releases found revenue only. PubMed real-world studies are single-centre outcome series (PMIDs 41708474, 40916321, 42733650, 42431171, 40270982), none reporting a share of eligible patients treated. (3) Revenue does not reconcile. product_revenue.csv shows Elahere US 477 (FY2024), 607 (FY2025) and 160 and 161 in Q1 and Q2 2026, flat since H1 2025 (303 vs 321 in H1 2026). At WAC $6,487.15 a vial x 3 to 4 vials x a real-world median of 8 cycles (Smick et al. 2025, PMID 40916321, n = 41), a course is $155,692 to $207,589. The annualised $642mm then implies 3,093 to 4,124 courses a year, more at net. The FRa-high share of the book's PROC pool is 4,382 x 36.3% = 1,591 (Previs et al. 2024, PMID 39631181, FRa-high in 36.3% of 425 Labcorp tests). The solved share is 1.9 to 2.6, above 100%. Part of the gap is off-label use: in a 66-patient real-world cohort only 52% of Elahere patients were platinum-resistant and 77% FRa-positive (PMID 42733650). Even at 52%, the count is 1,608 to 2,144, still at or above the pool. (4) Elahere is not this asset's rival for the slot anyway: MAESTRA 2 requires prior mirvetuximab in FRa-positive disease (TPS5642), so Elahere is the line before. The fair analogues are single-agent chemotherapy and Lifyorli, launched 2026-03-25 with no uptake data yet. The 'next step' in the note stands: load J9063 from the CMS Part B file. The book's AZD5335 row carries an unsourced 0.30 and should not be borrowed.

ramp_steepness.source: Book's Enhertu launch fit, as carried by the AZD5335 and sofetabart seeds in this disease: CMS Part B beneficiaries of 864, 1,904, 4,841, 7,105 and 8,410 over 2020 to 2024 (lookup.py demand Enhertu) give k = 1.08 with a midpoint at 2.2 years
ramp_steepness.note: Reused from the closest modelled competitors, the two ADC seeds in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. Case for slower: a new IHC test is needed before first use, and Elahere and Lifyorli will already hold the line. Case for faster: oral dosing against IV chemotherapy, and a biomarker most patients in this line carry at the trial cutoff
ramp_steepness.check: lookup.py demand Enhertu: Part B beneficiaries 864, 1,904, 4,841, 7,105 and 8,410 for 2020 to 2024, as cited. lookup.py seed AZD5335 and Sofetabart Mipitecan both carry k = 1.08 and midpoint 2.2 from that fit.

ramp_midpoint_year.note: Reused from the AZD5335 and sofetabart seeds
ramp_midpoint_year.check: Same Enhertu fit: midpoint 2.2 years on the AZD5335 and sofetabart seeds (lookup.py seed).
